claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you would like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to claim for my child Alex. Alex is 16 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 16 years old, I need to ask: is Alex currently in approved education or training? This would include things like:
- Full-time non-advanced education (e.g., A-levels, NVQs up to level 3)
- Approved training schemes (not provided by an employer)

Could you let me know Alex's current education or training status?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in education - doing A-levels at the local sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you. A-levels at sixth form college counts as approved full-time education.

Now I have a couple more questions about your circumstances:

Are you responsible for Alex? This generally means Alex lives with you, or you contribute at least the same amount as the Child Benefit rate towards looking after them.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

Are you and Alex living in the United Kingdom (England, Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, we live in England - in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you. One final question:

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone else recently claimed Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for all that information. Based on what you've told me and the eligibility rules, I now have everything I need to make an assessment.

Let me summarise your situation:
- Alex is 16 years old
- Alex is in approved full-time education (A-levels at sixth form college)
- Alex lives with you in England
- You are responsible for Alex
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! Based on the information you've provided, **you appear to be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

- **Age requirement**: Although the standard Child Benefit age limit is under 16, you can continue to receive Child Benefit for a child under 20 if they remain in approved education or training. Since Alex is 16 and studying A-levels at sixth form college, this counts as approved full-time education.

- **Responsibility**: You are responsible for Alex as they live with you.

- **Residence**: You both live in the UK (England).

- **No duplicate claims**: No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

If you'd like to make a claim, you can do so through the official government channels. Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
